data.reasoning: The PKGBUILD fetches a source tarball from the official VSCodium GitHub releases using a pinned SHA-256 checksum, and sources build scripts from within that verified tarball. The remaining files are standard desktop entries, metadata, and documentation. There is no malicious code or suspicious network activity. The disagreement was purely due to an API failure in one of the models, not a substantive security concern.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 API errors when attempting to audit three low-risk files (BUILDING, .gitignore, vscodium-uri-handler.desktop), which caused it to return an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and correctly identified the package as safe.
coverage_issues: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to audit 3 files (BUILDING, .gitignore, vscodium-uri-handler.desktop) due to LLM API errors (HTTP 400).
learnings: Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for transient LLM API errors (e.g., HTTP 400) to prevent minor files from causing an overall inconclusive verdict.

Consider implementing a risk-weighted verdict system: failures on low-risk, non-executable files (like .gitignore or .desktop) should not block a safe verdict if the high-risk files (PKGBUILD, .install) are verified safe.
